tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd — no broad macro or Fed commentary in today's dispatch, so let's go straight to the stories that matter.

The biggest pre-market mover is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug, showing 22% weight loss. That is a significant clinical milestone and puts Viking squarely in the conversation as a legitimate competitor in the obesity drug space. Watch the GLP-1 names broadly for sympathy moves.

On AutoZone — the headline beat looks good, fiscal Q4 EPS of 56 dollars and 5 cents versus the Street at 54 dollars and 3 cents, but peel it back and the quality is poor. About 145 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit. Strip those out and the beat shrinks considerably. More importantly, domestic comps were only up 1.6% versus the Street's 3.1% expectation, and the opex ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year. Management says sales linearity improved in the back half of the quarter and they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed print at best.

MillerKnoll delivered a cleaner beat — fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and critically, even backing out an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. That matters. Sales did miss, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year over year. The company trimmed the top end of full-year sales guidance but left the EPS range unchanged. Underlying earnings power looks intact.

THOR Industries is the clear disappointment. Fiscal Q4 EPS of 78 cents missed the 87-cent estimate and gross margins collapsed 230 basis points to 12.4%. Management's commentary was cautious — citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets through the critical RV selling season. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance was provided. The bright spots are dealer inventory at healthy levels and a roughly 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog year over year, but the headline results and qualitative tone are a headwind for the stock today.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus about 106 million more. RealSense is expected to do 80 to 90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year over year. This plants Cognex directly in the Physical AI buildout thematic, which is a strategically interesting move.

And Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He brings prior CFO experience at major industrials. Orderly transition, nothing alarming.

Bottom line for today — VKTX is the headline catalyst and a genuine positive. THO is the clearest fundamental disappointment. AZO and MLKN are mixed-to-slightly-positive stories depending on how much weight you give earnings quality. Macro context is absent from this note so watch the tape and overnight futures for your broader directional read heading into the open.
